center_bear_left_5mm_sweep.model_scope: continuous frozen tetrahedral body versus MuJoCo convex collision solids
limitations: Does not predict deformation, friction, grasp retention or contact forces.
Robot convex envelopes can overestimate nonconvex native collision surfaces.
Left pose is fixed at measured q; native affine compliance and future tracking are not included.
Only the declared straight translation segment is certified; other segments and obstacles require separate gates.
The certificate is for frozen-shape Cartesian translation, not continuous FK tracking of an interpolated joint trajectory.
A fresh actual-shape check remains necessary after physical preparation.

A changed handle material alters the native cloth dynamics; all phase gates must be recomputed from fresh actual observations.
No force, strain, grip retention, real final containment, release, or settled success is demonstrated.
All 8mm rigid failures are kept as failures. Diagnostic continuation through a blocked hypothetical segment only localizes remaining obstacles and does not authorize execution.
Frozen bear-left clearance is continuous for the declared translation; robot clearance and Cartesian tracking are sampled at 401 points.
